title: Falcon and the MJ-12 films from DIA HUMINT and Angleton's chop shop
summary: Eric Davis tells of Falcon and the MJ-12 films from DIA HUMINT and Angleton's chop shop, about 1980s at Defense Intelligence Agency, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: senior falcon was a DIA uh officer who was sent to communicate with Jamie Shandere and Bill Moore. He's the one that passed undeveloped 35mm film of the so-called MJ12 documents. These are the first generation documents that were created by James Jesus Angleton's chop shop, his his mole hunting document production factory.
Majestic 12 documents first appeared in 1984 in a film canister to UFO reason or to TV producer Jamie Chandere and this included the Eisenhower briefing document
tellings.difference: Dates the arrival to 1984 and names the Eisenhower Briefing Document and the Special Operations Manual. It says nothing about Falcon, the DIA or Angleton's chop shop as the source.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the first MJ-12 documents reaching Jaime Shandera on film in the 1980s. The Falcon story tells of the same handover of undeveloped 35mm film.

as_told.title: Majestic 12 documents arrive in a film canister

related.note: Both are about how the first MJ-12 documents reached Shandera and Moore in the 1980s. This telling says they were probably sent from near Kirtland, in Doty's orbit; the story says DIA's Falcon passed on film made by Angleton's chop shop.
Both concern Angleton's part in the MJ12 documents. This telling says Angleton probably leaked them, per Malmgren; the story says his chop shop made them and a DIA officer passed them on.

plain: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon research, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that in the 1980s an officer of the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military spy agency, code-named Falcon, was sent to meet two UFO researchers, Jaime Shandera and Bill Moore. Davis says Falcon gave them undeveloped 35mm film of the MJ-12 documents, papers that describe a supposed secret group of officials handling crashed UFOs. He says these first versions were made in the document factory of James Jesus Angleton, a famous CIA mole hunter, which would mean the famous papers came out of an intelligence operation.
